summary: Multiple metrics show extreme spikes and strong positive relationships during the 14:00‑14:08 window: external tax latency and checkout latency both jumped to 30 000 ms, gateway 504 error rate rose to 92 %, and blocked worker threads increased to 30. Correlation analysis reveals very high Pearson r values (>0.9) linking these metrics, indicating they moved together in this period.

evidence.interpretation: Latency for external tax service spiked to 30 000 ms, far above the baseline mean of 46.5 ms (z≈19969).
95th‑percentile checkout latency spiked to 30 000 ms, orders of magnitude above the typical 66.5 ms baseline (z≈19956).
Gateway 504 error percentage surged to 92 %, whereas baseline is essentially 0 %.
Error rate exceeds the defined alert threshold of 90 %.
Count of blocked worker threads rose to 30, well above the baseline mean of 2.
Gateway 504% shifted from a baseline mean of 0 % to a period mean of 41.25 %, a delta of 41.25 %.
Very strong positive correlation (r≈0.99) between blocked threads and checkout latency over the 8‑minute window.
High correlation (r≈0.97) linking external tax latency with blocked worker threads.
Strong correlation (r≈0.95) between checkout latency spikes and gateway 504 error rate.
